sources.frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Version the upload policy against the dated API references and retain explicit citations for privacy and quota instead of copying inherited summaries. Search-result summaries were used only for discovery; factual findings below come from fetched official pages.
sources.limitations: Null source dates mean no date was established; they are not guessed dates. No archived snapshot establishes the exact change date for every present-day statement. No assertion is made that an account has any particular quota, role or capability.

observed_facts: The API video resource has a stable video id and snippet.channelId identifying the channel to which the video was uploaded; the reference notes that channelId can change if a video is reassigned. These are distinct from a local filename, render, production or project identity.

videos.insert uploads to the channel associated with the authorized request. Its ordinary writable metadata does not provide a general-purpose destination-channel override. onBehalfOfContentOwnerChannel is explicitly for YouTube content partners, requires onBehalfOfContentOwner, a linked CMS identity and a channel linked to that content owner.

channels.list with mine=true requires authorization and returns channels owned by the authenticated user; managedByMe is a different partner-only filter. A public channel lookup by handle or ID does not itself prove upload authority.

Studio documents one active channel at a time and checking the name/icon to confirm the current channel. Closing an upload window before choosing visibility saves the video as private on the Content page; Checks can continue in the background.

The assignment supplies the FrameForge baseline: its publish stage opens a browser upload session or stages a queue item. This was not independently inspected and is not evidence that a YouTube resource was created or published.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Keep production ID, approved render identity, destination channel ID, authorization reference, upload attempt ID and returned YouTube video ID separate, linked records. Display the exact production/render and channel together when entering delivery.

[INFERENCE] Perform an authorized channel identity check before upload and compare the returned video snippet.channelId after upload with the approved destination. Do not rely on an email address, channel title, browser profile or copied channel URL as authority.

[INFERENCE] Preserve the production selection and delivery record when opening Studio, but call the state handoff-opened or queued until independent upload evidence is recorded. A locally opened window cannot establish remote completion.
project_context.limitations: No live channel identity or saved-context continuity was tested. The API and Studio are delivery surfaces, not a documented shared project/timeline system for FrameForge.

observed_facts: Not applicable as a native node-graph product: videos.insert is an HTTP operation and Studio uses staged forms, not a typed production DAG.

The resumable protocol starts with an authorized POST using uploadType=resumable and selected parts; a successful initialization returns 200 and a Location session URI. Media is sent by PUT to that URI. Successful complete transfer returns 201 and a video resource, not proof that processing or publication is complete.

After interruption, query the existing session with an empty PUT, Content-Length: 0 and Content-Range: bytes */TOTAL. A completed session returns the original final response; an incomplete one returns 308 and a zero-based Range. Resume at the next byte after the last acknowledged byte, not the last locally sent byte. Missing Range means no bytes have been acknowledged.

The guide specifies exponential backoff for resumable 500, 502, 503 and 504 responses and honoring Retry-After. Sessions expire; 404 for an expired session requires a new session and complete restart. Chunking is discouraged unless needed, and non-final chunks must use a consistent size that is a multiple of 256 KB.

videos.list can return owner-authorized processingDetails. processingStatus values are processing, succeeded, failed and terminated; terminated means processing information is no longer available. Processing progress is an estimate that can decrease when estimated work grows. uploadStatus separately supports uploaded, processed, failed, rejected and deleted, with conditional failure/rejection reasons.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Model local queueing, resumable initialization, byte transfer, upload receipt, processing, checks/review, scheduling and verified visibility as distinct states. Store the returned ID and reconcile the existing session before starting a new attempt to avoid accidental duplicate uploads.

[INFERENCE] Bind session URI and byte offset to the exact approved render and authorization/channel record; protect the session URI as operationally sensitive. Resume only unchanged bytes. Cancellation of a local job must not be represented as deletion of an already-created remote video.

[INFERENCE] Expose retryable transport failure, permanent metadata/authorization failure, upload-limit rejection and processing failure separately. Poll owner-only processing data with an appropriate consented scope and retain timestamps; progress is not a reliable monotonically increasing percentage.
node_execution.limitations: [uncertain] The inspected guide does not specify an exact resumable-session lifetime or an explicit server-side session-cancellation contract. No transfer, interruption, cancellation or recovery was exercised; these are documented capabilities, not FrameForge implementation evidence.

observed_facts: Uploading is not a footage-discovery or licensed-download workflow. The general API video resource describes metadata, license and file properties, not a complete provenance or rights-clearance record for all source assets.

The API status.license values are youtube and creativeCommon. Help states the standard YouTube license is the default and a Creative Commons Attribution license permits reuse subject to CC BY terms; attribution should identify title, author, source URL and license. CC licensing can only be applied when the content is eligible, and a Content ID claim prevents adding that license.

YouTube Help expressly says YouTube cannot grant rights to use content that someone else uploaded. Public visibility, a matching channel name, a Content ID result and permission to reuse source footage are different facts.

contentDetails.licensedContent means uploaded to a channel linked to a YouTube content partner and claimed by that partner. It is not a machine-readable blanket permission for a FrameForge user to download, edit or redistribute the footage.

Studio copyright Checks can detect claimed material and offer removal or dispute flows, but the results are not final: future manual claims, strikes or settings changes may affect the video. Private videos can also be reviewed for copyright and abuse.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Carry source URLs, rights documents, attribution obligations, permitted derivative/distribution uses and render-to-source references into approval. Do not replace that evidence with uploaded-video license flags or a passed copyright check.

[INFERENCE] Keep a rights-approval state separate from YouTube Checks and preserve claim/dispute outcomes as review evidence without automatically asserting legal clearance. Do not infer download permission from public availability.
footage_provenance.limitations: Not applicable for footage acquisition: no footage was searched, downloaded, imported or licensed, and no particular copyright claim or asset permission was assessed.

observed_facts: The documented desktop upload flow is Studio sign-in, CREATE > Upload videos, file selection, Details, applicable monetization/ad-suitability stages, Video elements, Checks and Visibility. Up to 15 videos may be selected at a time, with details editable for each file.

Details include title, description, thumbnail, playlist, audience and advanced metadata. Video elements include captions, cards and end screens. Checks run in the background and users can return later; publication is allowed while copyright checks are still running.

The Content page provides uploaded videos and a Visibility control. Uploading imports the file; publishing makes it available for anyone to watch. Studio can publish once SD processing is complete; HD/4K processing can take longer depending on length, format, quality and traffic.

The API exposes structured metadata and remote lifecycle state but does not supply a source bin, preview monitor, editing timeline, inspector or production graph. The cited upload workflow does not document a compositing/editing workspace or continuous selection shared with an external editor.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Keep preview, render identity, metadata, destination and upload/processing/checks receipts in one production inspector. Opening Studio should preserve the current production context locally but show a clear external handoff boundary.

[INFERENCE] Permit a return from the browser handoff to the same delivery panel without marking the whole production complete. Separate SD-ready publication eligibility from target-quality readiness if the approved output requires HD/4K.
editing_workspace.limitations: Documented flow only; no UI, window layout, persistence, upload dialog, thumbnail preview or cross-surface selection behavior was observed in an authenticated session.

observed_facts: Studio REUSE DETAILS copies selected details from a previously uploaded video. Help describes copying, not a live-linked or version-pinned production template.

Channel Upload defaults can set privacy, category, title, tags, comments, language and other defaults. Help limits their effect to browser uploads on youtube.com/upload; uploads through mobile or video editors do not respect those defaults. They must not be treated as the API request contract.

Studio channel permissions allow managers and editors to upload/publish subject to role limits. Invited users cannot access YouTube APIs through those channel permissions. A Studio invitation therefore is not equivalent to an OAuth upload grant.

OAuth authorization scopes govern API actions performed for the authorizing user. videos.insert accepts youtube.upload, youtube, youtubepartner or youtube.force-ssl. Server-side OAuth supports refresh tokens and background access after consent. The service-account exception is limited to qualifying content owners and onBehalfOfContentOwner methods, not ordinary channels.

A partner destination parameter or a copied channel-branded template does not replace CMS linkage and authorization requirements. The active browser channel can differ from a locally selected production channel.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Reuse metadata/branding definitions separately from each delivery instance. Snapshot their resolved version and explicit privacy/disclosure decisions into the approved instance rather than silently applying later template edits.

[INFERENCE] Scope credential references, authorization state, expected channel ID and remote video IDs to a channel-bound delivery configuration. Never embed tokens in reusable templates, clone credentials when duplicating a production, or fall back to another channel when permission checks fail.

[INFERENCE] Offer separate capability indicators for Studio delegate upload and API OAuth upload. Request only the scopes needed for the planned uploader plus identity/read-back operations, and verify granted permissions instead of assuming upload-only consent covers every inspection call.
template_channel_reuse.limitations: No credentials or actual roles were inspected. Exact scope selection and token-channel binding for FrameForge require implementation validation; this research establishes the documented separation, not operational connectivity.

observed_facts: CURRENT API PRIVACY CONTRACT: The fetched videos.insert and video schema explicitly document status.privacyStatus values private, public and unlisted. If omitted in videos.insert, privacyStatus defaults to public; certain uploads may default to private based on creator account settings. Both references explicitly state that videos uploaded from unverified API projects are not restricted to private viewing. An old blanket private-only assertion is not the current documented rule.

STUDIO DEFAULTS: Current Help says creators aged 13-17 default to private and creators 18 or older default to public. Closing the upload window before completing Visibility saves the video as private. Browser Upload defaults can also configure privacy. These distinct cases are not a safe substitute for explicitly specifying and reading back the intended visibility.

CURRENT API QUOTA: videos.insert has its own Video Uploads bucket with default 100 calls per day and costs 1 unit per call. search.list separately has a default 100 calls per day. All other endpoints share a default 10,000 units per day. Invalid requests incur at least one quota point and daily quotas reset at midnight Pacific Time. videos.list and channels.list cost 1 unit each in their applicable bucket. Additional quota requires an audit request; the actual project's allocation was not inspected.

DATED CHANGES IN WINDOW: Revision history December 4, 2025 says upload cost changed from approximately 1600 to approximately 100 units. June 1, 2026 announces granular buckets for videos.insert and search.list. The current 2026-10-15 references establish the present 1-unit/100-call upload contract. Neither the old 1600 nor the intermediate approximately 100 upload-unit cost should be presented as current.

CHANNEL LIMITS ARE DISTINCT: Studio Help documents a daily per-channel upload limit shared across desktop, mobile and API, without publishing one universal numeric allowance on that page. videos.insert documents uploadLimitExceeded. Studio's 15 files at a time is a batch-selection allowance, not an API quota or a daily channel upload allowance. API media size is capped at 256 GB with video/* or application/octet-stream MIME types.

DESTINATION AND PERMISSION: An API key or public channel lookup is not sufficient for upload. OAuth requires user consent and an accepted videos.insert scope. The channel is associated with the authorized request unless the strictly qualified content-partner parameters apply. Studio manager/editor permission does not confer YouTube API access. Public OAuth apps using scopes for certain user data require Google's verification process; that is separate from the upload privacy statement above.

PROCESSING AND CHECKS: The complete resumable transfer returns 201 plus the video resource. That resource is not a guarantee that processing succeeded, copyright checks completed, or a video is public. Owner-authorized processingDetails tracks processing; status.uploadStatus and failure/rejection reasons describe separate outcomes. Studio allows publication after SD processing, including while copyright Checks continue. Copyright results are expressly nonfinal. Current upload Help also documents a background likeness-detection scan, with no immediate visibility restriction from that check alone and possible later removal for policy violations.

SCHEDULING: status.publishAt can only be set while privacyStatus is private and the video has never been published. When updating publishAt, privacyStatus must also explicitly be private. A publishAt time in the past publishes immediately. Studio scheduling keeps the video private until the chosen date; a Community Guidelines penalty can prevent the scheduled publication and require rescheduling afterward.

DISCLOSURE BASELINE: The October 30, 2024 revision entry introduced status.containsSyntheticMedia for realistic altered/synthetic content; this is historical baseline outside the requested window but remains present in current insert/update schemas. Current specialized Help requires disclosure for realistic AI-generated/meaningfully altered content, including depictions of real people doing things they did not do, altered real events/places, realistic fabricated scenes, and AI music that is the main focus. Production assistance, captions, minor aesthetic edits and clearly unrealistic content do not automatically require disclosure. The examples are not exhaustive.

CURRENT DISCLOSURE WORKFLOW: The specialized Help page describes Attributes > AI use > Yes/No and player/description labels, including automatic labels from YouTube AI tools, C2PA metadata or internal detection. Disclosing alone does not limit audience or monetization eligibility; repeated nondisclosure may lead to labels, removal or Partner Program suspension. The general upload Help still uses the wording Altered content under advanced details. These are documented wording differences, not an observed account-specific UI.

READ-BACK CONTRACT: videos.list can retrieve by the returned video id with parts snippet,status,processingDetails,contentDetails. snippet.channelId identifies the uploaded-to channel; status.privacyStatus is the current visibility; status.publishAt is scheduling intent; status.containsSyntheticMedia is the relevant API disclosure property; processingDetails is owner-only. FileDetails and suggestions are also owner-only. publishedAt alone is not proof of a public state: private owner queries and unlisted uploads have documented upload-time cases.

VISIBILITY SEMANTICS: Public videos may appear on the channel and in search. Unlisted videos can be watched and reshared by anyone with the link and can surface through a public playlist; they are not private. Private videos are visible only to the owner and selected people, although YouTube systems/reviewers can inspect them. Studio's Content > Visibility is the documented human-readable setting location.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Approve an immutable delivery manifest containing the exact render/hash, metadata revision, destination channel ID, explicit requested privacyStatus, schedule/timezone interpretation, audience setting, AI-use decision and rights evidence. A render or delivery-metadata change invalidates that approval; neither YouTube upload method defines FrameForge's approval invalidation rules.

[INFERENCE] Use an explicitly chosen private upload for review when that is the approved workflow, rather than relying on an assumed private default. Never silently omit privacyStatus. Reconfirm the destination and user-approved visibility before any separate public/unlisted transition; unlisted is still externally shareable.

[INFERENCE] Distinguish approval granted, queued, handoff opened, transfer underway, upload receipt received, processing, checks pending/reviewed, scheduled and visibility verified. Keep a browser handoff or local queue item at its truthful state. A publication badge requires timestamped remote video ID/channel ID/privacy read-back matching the approved manifest, not an open browser or a local success flag.

[INFERENCE] API verification sequence for a future authorized implementation: establish expected channel using an authenticated identity query; explicitly send part=snippet,status and status.privacyStatus; capture the remote receipt ID; then read the exact ID using videos.list and compare snippet.channelId and current privacyStatus, capture upload/processing failure or rejection, and re-read after any scheduled or explicit visibility transition. Missing resources, missing fields or authorization errors mean verification is unresolved, not success.

[INFERENCE] Do not equate processingStatus=succeeded with copyright clearance or universal watchability. Retain Studio Checks review separately from Data API processing status; retain policy/region restrictions and the time of visibility verification. If copyright review is a FrameForge publication gate, enforce it locally because Studio permits publishing while Checks are pending.

[INFERENCE] Track project upload quota separately from channel daily limits and the shared read-back quota. Surface quota exhaustion as a blocked delivery, not a reason to switch projects/channels or repeatedly create new uploads. Reconcile resumable sessions before retrying after an ambiguous final response.
limitations: [uncertain] The exact effective date when the current public default/unverified-project privacy wording replaced any older restriction was not established by the inspected revision entries. Current direct references agree on the current rule; do not invent a dated repeal.

[uncertain] Current general-upload and specialized disclosure Help use different UI labels, and the Data API property's text focuses on realistic altered/synthetic media without spelling out a separate AI-music-primary-focus setting. The exact account UI and API parity for every current music-label scenario were not established; preserve a human disclosure review instead of inventing an API field.

[uncertain] The inspected Data API schema does not establish a complete ordinary-creator Studio copyright-Checks status/read-back endpoint. Processing status, rejectionReason and licensedContent must not be repurposed as a clean copyright-check result.

No actual quota allocation, OAuth grant, channel permission, upload, copyright scan, processing result, disclosure label, scheduling action or public visibility was tested. Post-action read-back is a recommended design contract, not an action performed in this research.

observed_facts: General YouTube screen-reader Help documents keyboard-enabled search and player interactions, including the slash key for search, keyboard seeking, captions and Escape from full screen. This page is about YouTube search/playback, not a complete Studio upload accessibility specification.

Upload Help publishes separate computer, Android and iPhone/iPad instructions, and current disclosure Help supports a computer or mobile Studio AI-use setting. Channel-permission documentation also distinguishes supported actions across desktop Studio, Studio app and YouTube. These are platform-specific workflows, not evidence of identical responsive layout or feature parity.
The upload API is nonvisual. It supplies status data that a client can render, but does not provide focus handling, announcements, keyboard navigation or responsive UI behavior.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Build an independently accessible delivery inspector: semantic labeled channel/visibility/disclosure controls, keyboard-operable review and cancel actions, focus restoration after external handoff, announced upload/processing failures and progress, and status labels that do not depend on color alone.

[INFERENCE] Keep destination, render revision and requested visibility visible in condensed layouts and disclose the platform-specific nature of any Studio handoff. Validate keyboard, screen-reader and narrow-screen behavior separately from API correctness.
accessibility_responsiveness.limitations: [uncertain] Studio-upload-specific focus order, screen-reader announcements, small-screen reflow and WCAG conformance were not established by the public sources inspected. The generic screen-reader Help contains retained legacy references and cannot certify the current Studio uploader. No browser or accessibility/runtime test was performed.
